bibl.title: After the heliacal rising of Sirius: Sothic symbols, celestial bodies and zodiacal signs on Roman Provincial coins of Alexandria.
bibl.seg: Yannis Stoyas, After the heliacal rising of Sirius: Sothic symbols, celestial bodies and zodiacal signs on Roman Provincial coins of Alexandria.
Nέδα [Neda Annual Yearbook, University of the Peloponnese] 2 (2017-2018 [2020]) pp. 441-473, figg.; - 864.
bibl.note: Coin issues of Alexandria under Antoninus Pius (AD 138-161) showcase highly interesting themes with astronomical / astrological connotations. More specifically, in 144/5 a coin series was produced with all the signs of the Zodiac; each zodiacal sign is paired with one of the then known "planets". This series was supplemented with four relevant issues, on which the principal iconographic element is the Zodiac wheel. The reasons for the extensive use of this peculiar iconography have to be sought in a preceding pivotal event: in July 139 AD the closure and renewal of a Sothic period (= 1461 Egyptian years, corresponding to 1460 Julian years) had occurred. After so long a time the phenomenon of the heliacal rising of Sirius (which was important for the inhabitants of Egypt) coincided with the opening of the new year -1st of the month Thoth, according to the Egyptian calendar. The significance of the event was marked down already in the 2nd year of Antoninus (138/9) on an Alexandrian issue where the representation of the mythical phoenix was accompanied by the legend ΑΙΩΝ. The recurrence of this theme in the 6th year of Antoninus (142/3) has a sound explanation: in that year Sirius would rise on the first day of the Egyptian year for the last time. The appearance of the zodiacal issues of Alexandria in 144/5 is most probably associated with the marriage of Marcus Aurelius and Faustina the Younger; it had been set after Antoninus ascended the throne (July 138) and it took place in April (or May) 145.
